accuracy.evidence: Matched to NC KS3 English reading (read critically; know how language, vocabulary choice, grammar and text structure present meaning; study texts from different times) and CCSS RI.6.6–RI.8.6. Facts checked: the Chicxulub impact is dated to about 66 million years ago; the Titanic sailed from Southampton on 10 April 1912 and sank in the early hours of 15 April 1912; 'practically unsinkable' is the description The Shipbuilder printed in 1911; sea turtles are documented mistaking plastic bags for jellyfish; microplastics are particles under 5 mm. The charity figures ('millions of tonnes', '2 tonnes cleared') are given as an example leaflet, not as a claim about a real charity. Numeric items computed by hand at their corners.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented KS3 slips: judging audience by topic rather than language (dinosaurs means children, tag topic; Year 8 letter means pupils), assuming a text full of facts only informs (tag facts), reading hedging as ignorance (tag hedge), judging an old text by present knowledge (Titanic, tag context), mixing up form and audience (tag form), and mistaking headline capitals for data (tag conv).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagpac works on one fact written for three readers: drag-to-reader matching, convention chips in a report sentence, a three-slot register builder that must fit two different briefs, a primary-purpose line finder, a timeline drop for a 1912 clipping and a P/A/C chooser for a school letter. flagpurp is the ages 7–9 persuade/inform/entertain sorter, flagreg swaps formal and informal words and flagdial covers dialects; the shingle gate is under 30% against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step makes the learner do the analysis before the rule is confirmed: matching fails with a message naming the giveaway features, the chip step lists each convention as it is found, the rewrite step only completes when all three parts fit the reader (so the learner sees the fact stay fixed while register changes), the leaflet step rejects fact lines with 'Facts can serve persuasion', and the timeline step rejects 'after it sank' by pointing at the date.

predictions.evidence: Six predictions with tempting wrong options: 'B: it has the most dramatic words' for the scientists' text, 'The writer is unsure of the facts' for 'suggesting', 'The fact itself' for rewriting for 6-year-olds, 'To inform: it is full of facts' for the leaflet, 'The writer was joking' for 'practically unsinkable' and 'Year 8 pupils' for the letter's audience.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge texts, each with two tagged wrong options; nine distinct messages name the slip with the text's own words, e.g. 'The topic does not decide the audience. The language does: “isotopic” and “indicates” are for experts.' and 'Form is the kind of text; audience is the reader.'

readability.evidence: The first validate run reported kid FK 5.8 against a 5.0 target; the kid paragraphs were rewritten with shorter sentences and now pass, still using the KS3 terms purpose, audience, context and the named conventions. Adult text names the programme of study and CCSS codes and lists four common mistakes.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate clean. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (the three questions, one fact many versions, language not topic, two purposes and context), and each lab step practises one of them; the numeric items each carry a reading point in their explanation (exact data vs headline, date of writing, call to action).

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 dark and 360 px Android light screenshots after Show me on every step: the canvas is 1.25 tall on phones so wrapped text cards, chips and the clue list fit without clipping; canvas text is 12.5 px minimum with bold weights; every action also has a DOM button (wrapping in rows), and the clue buttons now drop out as clues are found.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin (Text A/B/C then reader, one button per word chip, Change the opening/subject/ending, Line 1–4, Before/After it sank, Next purpose/audience/context); the canvas aria-label carries every spoken result including the challenge text and feedback; walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone.
